title: done --note and note mean different things (log vs slice)
findings_note: dogfooding S18: 'done --note' writes only log.jsonl; 'slicer note' writes the slice. Same word, two destinations — easy to confuse. Align naming/help, or surface log notes somewhere visible.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
`done/start/park/unpark --note` records a one-line history/log entry; `slicer note` appends a
durable dated note on the item (shown in show/render). Both said "note" and the flag help read
"one line for the log", which is easy to confuse. Filed dogfooding S18.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- src/slicer/cli.py: reword the four `--note` help strings.
- README.md; a help-content test in tests/test_cli.py.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Clarify only (no behavior change): the four status `--note` flags now read "one line recorded in
history (see `slicer note` for a durable note on the item)"; the README done/park/unpark row
distinguishes the two. Flag name, behavior, and JSON are unchanged; log notes remain viewable via
`slicer log --item`.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
`slicer done --help` mentions history and `slicer note`; `done --note` behaves as before. Focused
help test + the unit suite.
